classification.difficultyReason: Test which labelled sectors actually exhaust a straight angle without inferring unmarked relationships.

content.prompt: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

spec.description: One horizontal baseline, two dashed upper rays, a° in the left outer sector and b° in the right outer sector; central sector unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled sectors do not exhaust the straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer shown. Source pink and green fills are replaced by unfilled sector arcs, pending presentation review.

answer.worked: An additional angle lies between the sloping rays, so $a$ and $b$ alone do not fill the straight angle. Correct answer: False.

answer.worked: The three adjacent angles fill a straight angle, so $a+b+c=180$. Correct answer: True.

answer.worked: The adjacent angles $a$ and $b$ fill a straight angle, so $a+b=180$. Correct answer: True.

answer.worked: $a+b=180$ because angles on a straight line add up to $180°$. Adding the positive angle $c$ gives $a+b+c>180$. Correct answer: False.
